notes: Today src/cli.mjs only prints the usage line and exits 2, and src/store.mjs does not exist: T1 creates it, T2 and T3 extend it. No dependency is added; package.json stays without one.

Storage (D2, spec A1): data/items.jsonl holds one JSON object per line, {"name":"<trimmed name>"}, written with appendFileSync. src/store.mjs owns the file: saveItem(name) appends one line; listItems() returns the names in file order, or [] when the file is missing. The path is resolved from the module (new URL("../data/items.jsonl", import.meta.url)), so add and list use the same file whatever the working directory. data/ is committed (data/.gitkeep) and data/items.jsonl is gitignored.

Errors: saveItem throws new Error("item name must not be blank") before writing when the name is blank under spec A2 (empty after trim(), or containing a line break); a missing argument is the empty string, so it is blank. src/cli.mjs wraps both commands in one try/catch: a thrown error prints its message to stderr and exits 1. The usage error keeps exit code 2.

Risks: a crash mid-append may leave a torn last line, and two processes appending at once may interleave lines; the spec assumes one process at a time (A3) and makes recovery a non-goal, so nothing is built for either, and a torn line makes list fail with its JSON error (exit 1) rather than print a partial item. A missing data/ folder would fail the append; data/.gitkeep keeps it in every checkout.

Checks: item-add (AC1), item-blank (AC2) and item-list (AC3) each start by removing data/items.jsonl and run every command as its own process, so each case starts from nothing and list reads from disk in a new process.
